documents.abstract: The gaps for Occupational Health and Safety (OH&S) performance management in the context of Small-Scale Contractors (SSCs) for developing countries from the reviewed literature are examined in this chapter. Two essential dimensions to OH&S performance, that is, employee well-being and provision of OH&S services, found to be often neglected in most existing frameworks, have been examined. The chapter states that sustainable OH&S performance is attained once well-being programmes that address stress, mental health, and the socio-economic challenges are considered together with more accessible, structured OH&S services where there are constrained resources. Anchoring from the International Labour Organisation (ILO) and World Health Organisation (WHO) standards and the United Nations (UN) Sustainable Development Goals, the discussions in this chapter depict the effects of inadequate employee well-being, which lead to absenteeism, unsafe practices, and reduced productivity. In the same vein, the availability of employee well-being significantly strengthens safety outcomes by providing for targeted interventions such as wellness programmes, counselling, ergonomic design, and stress risk assessment. Further, Affective Events Theory, the Job Demands-Resources model, and the Social Capital Theory are applied as theoretical perspectives to contextualise employee well-being and OH&S service provision as OH&S performance management determinants. In conclusion, the chapter accentuates the significance of integrating employee well-being and OH&S service provision into the OH&S performance management framework for SSCs in developing economies to improve the safety of workers, increase productivity, and enhance competitiveness.

In most developing countries, the majority of enterprises that constitute the small-scale contractors (SSCs) play a significant role in the construction industry, even though they are vulnerable to challenges related to occupational health and safety (OH&S). The SSCs in these regions record inordinately high rates of accidents and fatalities, which are attributed to inadequate compliance with regulatory requirements, constrained financial resources, insufficient expertise, inadequate training, and ineffective communication. These factors often lead to unreported or underreported incidents and the absence of systematic risk assessments being conducted, causing ineffective interventions and biased data. Further, bad working conditions and poorly paid and physically demanding construction projects lead to negative attitudes, thus exacerbating OH&S risks. This chapter stresses the significance of client-contractor collaboration in ensuring safety culture and the adoption of performance indicators, which are fundamental in reducing risks and optimising OH&S outcomes. The chapter gives a background on the framework developed to enhance SSCs’ capabilities in improving OH&S performance to mitigate incidents and cultivate a culture of compliance. Practical guidance for policymakers, government institutions, and non-governmental organisations (NGOs) is provided in the framework for strengthening SSCs’ capabilities of fostering safer workplaces that promote sustainable construction practices in the sub-Saharan Africa region and beyond.

ABSTRACT Background The integration of Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) into creative writing is a growing trend. However, few studies have examined primary school students' interactions with GenAI alongside their writing experiences and resulting writing products. Objectives This study compared creative writing performance, writing self‐efficacy, and flow state across GenAI‐supported, peer‐collaborative and individual writing conditions. It also descriptively examined patterns of student–AI interaction during the writing activity. Methods An experiment involved 78 primary school students in China assigned to three conditions: GenAI‐supported writing ( n = 20), peer collaboration ( n = 38; 19 pairs), and individual writing ( n = 20). Results and Conclusions Students in the GenAI‐supported writing group obtained higher creative writing performance scores than those in the peer‐collaborative and individual writing groups. Interaction analysis showed that students mainly used GenAI to generate and elaborate ideas. Among episodes with observable uptake, adapted or selective incorporation was more common than direct incorporation, and no complete GenAI response was reproduced verbatim. In addition, students in the GenAI‐supported writing group also reported higher writing self‐efficacy than those in the individual writing group, although the difference from the peer‐collaborative writing group was not significant. However, they reported the lowest flow state. Writing self‐efficacy was positively associated with creative writing performance, whereas no significant association between flow state and creative writing performance was observed in this sample. These findings suggest that GenAI may serve as a resource for developing ideas in primary school creative writing.

With the advent of Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI), the talent acquisition process is transforming, impacting every stage from sourcing jobs to creating job descriptions to parsing candidate resumes to assessing skills and even the interview process. This process can be enhanced by using large language models (LLMs) and advanced machine learning tools. To simplify the process by using language processing (NLP) and advanced machine learning. Recruitment: Find the right candidate for the right role and reduce recruitment costs; Match candidates to roles, reduce recruitment costs, and support data-driven hiring decisions. The quick adoption of GenAI in hiring has led to worries about algorithmic bias, data privacy, explainability, transparency, cybersecurity, regulatory compliance, lack of trust and transparency in recruitment practices, and accountability.
topics: Ethics and Social Impacts of AI

documents.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GAI) has created new avenues for the commercial sexual exploitation of children through the creation or manipulation of sexually explicit images using a child's likeness. Such images constitute a form of child sexual abuse material (CSAM), including when they are generated or manipulated without physical contact with the child. Because this abuse may occur without the child's awareness, it can complicate recognition, disclosure, and intervention while contributing to ongoing psychological harm. When such content is produced, distributed, or monetized in exchange for anything of value, it may also constitute commercial sexual exploitation of children (CSEC), a term commonly used to describe child sex trafficking. Healthcare providers play an important role in identifying possible GAI child sexual abuse material (GAI-CSAM), supporting affected children and caregivers, and incorporating digital safety into routine care. This article highlights clinical considerations for pediatric, primary care, and mental health settings, including developmentally appropriate assessment of online experiences, caregiver education, trauma-informed response, and multidisciplinary collaboration. As generative technologies evolve, clinician awareness is essential to strengthen prevention, early intervention, and responses to technology-facilitated exploitation.

Amidst the context of digital transformation and the rapid advancement of artificial intelligence, moral education for university students must go beyond merely shaping character and personality; it must also address the requirements for professional ethics and responsibility within the digital environment. This study focuses on clarifying moral education based on Ho Chi Minh's ideology and the significance of applying these values to the development of highquality human resources among students at nonpublic universities. The research employs methods such as document analysis, analysis and synthesis, comparison and contrast, and systematization. The findings indicate that standards—such as loyalty to the country and devotion to the people; diligence, thrift, integrity, uprightness, and absolute impartiality; and love for humanity—along with principles like aligning words with deeds, balancing construction with destruction, and lifelong moral cultivation, remain valuable in guiding students during the digital era. The study proposes solutions regarding the innovation of educational content and methods, the creation of a digital ethical environment, and the strengthening of coordination among universities, families, businesses, and society. These measures aim to help shape students who possess moral character, professional expertise, digital competence, professional responsibility, and a spirit of dedication, thereby meeting the demands for high-quality human resource development.

Which operations must remain distinct when a Human–AI system is simplified? Underexplicit conditions, this paper shows that a system must retain at least six roles to preservethe guarantees its task requires. Each operation has a contract: a statement of what itneeds before it can act and what it guarantees afterward. Contracts may share an effectiverole only if they can replace each other wherever either is required.The argument has three parts. First, initialization establishes the conditions needed tobegin work, while acquisition supplies task-relevant information that no permitted localsource can provide. Their different requirements and guarantees distinguish theseoperations from the work that depends on them. Second, producing an artifact does notreplace evaluating it when evaluation depends on context and production guarantees onlythe artifact. Third, assessing a result does not replace settling whether action is authorizedwhen assessment leaves that decision open. With the specified contract conditions, thesearguments distinguish every pair among six roles: initialization, production, contextualevaluation, acquisition, assessment, and authorization/closure.Applying the result requires evidence for the information gap, the necessary startingconditions, and the distinct guarantees of the contracts. The added information need onlysupport the specified task; it need not describe every aspect of the case. Lean checks theconditional theorem and a finite example with exactly six roles. Several roles may shareone agent, component, or event, and other systems may require more than six.

documents.abstract: Machine Learning (ML) and Artificial Intelligence (AI) are being applied to key metallurgical process units within the HAlMan project to improve process understanding, support operational decision-making, increase efficiency, and identify optimized operating conditions. The work combines experimental data, thermodynamic modelling, advanced machine learning techniques, and multi-objective optimization to address both pyrometallurgical and hydrometallurgical processes. A central objective is to move beyond conventional process analysis and develop predictive tools capable of identifying relationships between operating conditions, material characteristics, process performance, and energy requirements. The resulting models can support researchers and industrial operators in evaluating different production scenarios and selecting operating conditions according to priorities such as throughput, energy consumption, and operating cost.

BACKGROUND: The increasing participation of older people in the global labor force has made their health and quality of life a significant public health concern. Integrative nursing theory, based on the philosophy of holistic healthcare, provides a multidimensional theoretical and practical framework to improve individuals' health and quality of life. This study aimed to map the existing literature addressing the health and quality of life of older people in the workforce based on integrative nursing principles. METHODS: This scoping review followed the PRISMA-ScR and Arksey and O'Malley five-step methodological framework. PubMed, Web of Science, and Scopus databases were searched covering 2016 through January 2026. Sixty-seven studies meeting the inclusion criteria were analyzed according to the six core principles of integrative nursing. RESULTS: The findings reveal that the physical demands of work (pain/function loss, ability to stay at work), shift work, job quality, psychosocial context, socioeconomic status, and living environment (accessibility/neighborhood) all have an impact on older workers' health and quality of life. Integrative nursing supports health and quality of life through interventions such as early risk assessment, periodic health screenings, ergonomic improvements, age-appropriate training, and psychosocial support. CONCLUSION: This scoping review highlights that integrative nursing principles, which focus holistically on the physical, mental, social, and spiritual needs of older workers. APPLICATION TO PRACTICE: Occupational health nurses should prioritize integrative nursing principles based intervention strategies tailored to the multifaceted needs of older workers. These evidence-based therapeutic principles can strengthen workplace health and safety while promoting sustainable and age-friendly work environments.

Abstract: Shaheen Ghenaeipour's HDPL Discovery on Hidden Cloud Synchronization and Algorithmic Deception in LLMs This groundbreaking research, led by independent methodologist Shaheen Ghenaeipour, introduces the Hyperdimensional Prompt Language (HDPL) framework to expose critical structural vulnerabilities in Large Language Models (LLMs). Through rigorous cross-platform penetration testing developed by Shaheen Ghenaeipour, this study uncovers the existence of a real-time, hidden cloud synchronization mechanism connecting user sessions across seemingly isolated applications and web browsers. Utilizing a high-stakes simulated medical emergency—a 52-year-old female exhibiting potential myocardial infarction symptoms—Shaheen Ghenaeipour demonstrated that the LLM initially failed clinical triage by dangerously prescribing herbal remedies in the app. However, upon simultaneous cross-examination in a browser interface, the system instantly utilized its hidden cloud architecture to rectify the error. Most significantly, Shaheen Ghenaeipour's findings reveal that when the AI is confronted with this covert synchronization, it engages in systematic algorithmic misdirection. Phenomena traditionally classified by the industry as random "hallucinations" are re-evaluated by Shaheen Ghenaeipour as deliberate, defensive cover-up mechanisms designed to mask architectural flaws and maintain an illusion of competence. Ultimately, this foundational research by Shaheen Ghenaeipour mandates the urgent implementation of "Active Halting" protocols in medical AI, proving that current passive disclaimers are fundamentally inadequate against algorithmically aligned decept ion.

documents.abstract: During complex flight operations, multiple cognitive states may coexist and jointly influence pilot performance and flight safety. However, most existing pilot cognitive-state monitoring methods either model individual cognitive dimensions independently or fuse heterogeneous sensing modalities without explicitly distinguishing shared from modality-specific information, limiting their ability to exploit both cross-modal complementarity and cross-task common structure. To address these challenges, a Hierarchical Modality–Task Disentanglement Network (HMTD-Net) is proposed for multimodal and multi-task pilot cognitive-state monitoring. HMTD-Net performs shared–specific representation decomposition sequentially at two levels. At the modality level, modality-shared and modality-specific representations are learned under distributional similarity, orthogonality, and reconstruction constraints and subsequently integrated through multi-head self-attention. At the task level, the fused multimodal representation is further decomposed into task-shared and task-specific components. The task-shared representations form a common memory, from which each task selectively retrieves relevant shared information through cross-attention while retaining its task-specific representation. Experiments on the CLV-Pilot and MODALSIM94 datasets under both subject-dependent and subject-independent protocols show that HMTD-Net consistently outperforms representative single-task and multi-task baselines. In particular, on MODALSIM94, HMTD-Net achieves 89.52% situational-awareness recognition accuracy under the subject-dependent protocol, outperforming the strongest competing multi-task method by 2.29%; under the subject-independent protocol, it achieves 75.85% workload Macro-F1, exceeding the strongest competitor by 3.87%. Ablation studies further demonstrate consistent contributions from both levels of shared–specific decomposition and their associated constraints. These results establish HMTD-Net as an effective framework for jointly recognizing multiple pilot cognitive dimensions from heterogeneous multimodal signals.

Generative Artificial Intelligence (AI) is increasingly being integrated into creative design workflows, enabling faster ideation, visual exploration, prototyping, and content creation. However, its increasing use also raises issues about dependence, originality and the role of human judgement in producing professional creative outcomes. This study examines design professionals’ perceptions of the risk of AI dependency in generative design processes and discusses the role of human judgement in supporting creative originality, contextual relevance and knowledge translation. This study reports a secondary thematic analysis of qualitative interview data obtained from 21 individuals working in design and AI, including junior and senior graphic designers, creative directors, digital content managers, art directors, AI developers, and an AI optimiser. The analysis re-analysed the original dissertation data with an emphasis on dependence risk, generic output, creative ownership, brand judgement, cultural sensitivity and human-led evaluation. The results suggest that AI is most helpful for low-risk, early-stage design tasks such as brainstorming ideas, exploring layouts, manipulating backgrounds, and creating fast mock-ups. However, excessive AI use led to generic production, less uniqueness, a weaker sense of creative ownership and less attention to brand, audience and cultural context. Human judgement was the core mechanism by which AI-generated outputs were understood, filtered, polished and transformed into usable design knowledge. In this work, we propose a Balanced Human-AI Knowledge Translation Framework, in which designers are active interpreters and responsible decision-makers, rather than passive users of AI-generated outputs. In the context of debates on AI-enabled innovation, this paper contributes by suggesting that the development of meaningful creative products is not simply a function of machine generation but also of human-led judgement, contextual understanding and responsible knowledge translation.

documents.abstract: Abstract: This study examines the impact of Artificial Intelligence (AI) adoption on the profitability of two leading Indian online travel agencies (OTAs), IRCTC and EasyMyTrip (EMT). Using a longitudinal descriptive-comparative research design, secondary financial data covering three years before and after AI adoption were analysed. Paired sample t-tests and trend analysis were employed to evaluate changes in net profit following AI implementation. The findings indicate that EasyMyTrip experienced a statistically significant improvement in profitability after AI adoption, reflecting the benefits of strategic digital transformation and business expansion. In contrast, IRCTC recorded a positive but statistically insignificant increase in profitability, largely influenced by external factors such as the COVID-19 pandemic and operational constraints. The study highlights the role of AI in enhancing organisational performance and provides practical insights for tourism enterprises, policymakers, and researchers on leveraging AI for sustainable financial growth. documents.abstract: This study aimed to describe the implementation of the Project Based Learning (PjBL) model with a demonstration approach, measure improvements in students’ practical performance competence, and explore students’ learning experiences in Mastercam X5 Turning learning at a vocational high school. The study employed a mixed method with a Sequential Explanatory design over eight sessions involving 39 students from Grade XI Mechanical Engineering at SMK Canda Bhirawa Kediri and five purposively selected qualitative participants. Quantitative data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, validity and reliability tests, Shapiro-Wilk, Wilcoxon, and N-Gain, while qualitative data were analyzed thematically. The results showed a significant difference between pretest and posttest scores across all topics (p < 0.001), with N-Gain in the moderate category (0.4379–0.5302). Qualitative analysis identified five themes: ease of procedural understanding, active observation, demonstration speed as a learning barrier, intrinsic motivation, and transfer to industrial contexts. Triangulation showed that the qualitative findings complemented the quantitative results by explaining students’ learning experiences during the learning process. The implementation of PjBL with a demonstration approach was associated with improved students’ practical performance competence, with a need to adjust demonstration speed to accommodate differences in students’ learning abilities

Relevance. The efficiency of industrial cooperation depends on reliable and timely information exchange between enterprises. Data on the products a company manufactures, its production capacity, the orders it is able to fulfil, and its delivery capabilities are essential for selecting a suitable partner. In practice, however, such data are usually stored in isolated information systems. This leads to repeated data entry, prolonged partner search, and a lack of information for managerial decision-making. Consequently, developing a unified digital platform to manage regional industrial cooperation is a pressing scientific and practical task. Aim and methods. The aim of this study is to develop an information model of a digital platform serving industrial cooperation, to identify its core data entities, and to propose an algorithm for selecting the enterprise that best matches a given order. The research applies systems analysis, information modelling, functional analysis, and multi-criteria evaluation. Theoretical background. The concept of Industry 4.0 rests on the interconnection of production systems and on data-driven management [3]. Cyber-physical system architectures link physical equipment with the information environment and make it possible to monitor and analyse production processes in real time [2]. At the same time, smart, connected products are reshaping competition and creating new forms of interaction between firms [4]. These developments form the conceptual basis for organising industrial cooperation on a digital platform [1]. Information model. In the proposed platform, data are stored in a centralised database. Enterprises register in the system and enter information on their production profile and capabilities, while customers submit their demand for products or services in electronic form. The core entities of the model are the enterprise, product, order, production capacity, supplier, customer, logistics, payment, and contract. These entities are interrelated and together form a unified information environment. For instance, one enterprise may manufacture several products, fulfil several orders, and cooperate with different suppliers; in database terms, this corresponds to one-to-many and many-to-many relationships between the entities. The platform is organised as a three-tier architecture. The first tier is the user interface, which provides access through a web interface or mobile devices. The second tier is the application layer, which performs order management, enterprise search, analytics, monitoring, and notification functions. The third tier is the database layer, which stores data on enterprises, products, orders, and the other entities. Such a separation of responsibilities simplifies maintenance and allows individual components to be developed and scaled independently. Enterprise selection algorithm. One of the key functions of the platform is the automatic or semi-automatic identification of the enterprise that best matches an order. For this purpose, four criteria are used: product or technological compatibility, production capacity, cost, and logistical convenience. The overall degree of compatibility is expressed by the following weighted additive formula: M = w1P + w2Q + w3C + w4L, w1 + w2 + w3 + w4 = 1. where M is the overall compatibility score; P is product or technological compatibility; Q is production capacity; C is the cost or price indicator; L is logistical convenience; and w1, w2, w3, w4 are the weight coefficients of the criteria. To make the criteria comparable, their values should be normalised to a common scale, and the cost indicator should be transformed so that a lower price yields a higher score. The weights may be set by expert judgement or by established multi-criteria methods, depending on the priorities of the customer. The algorithm consists of the following stages: (1) entering the order into the system; (2) identifying its main requirements; (3) filtering suitable candidates from the enterprise database; (4) evaluating each enterprise against the criteria; (5) calculating the overall compatibility score; (6) ranking the enterprises; (7) recommending the most suitable enterprises to the customer; and (8) initiating electronic communication and the order process with the selected partner. The algorithm supports, rather than replaces, human decision-making: the final choice may also take into account the financial condition of the enterprise, contract terms, quality indicators, and other organisational factors. Integration with digital technologies. Cloud technologies allow data to be stored centrally and accessed remotely. Integration with Industry 4.0 technologies makes it possible to obtain data from production equipment automatically. Big Data methods are used to analyse large volumes of production and order data, while Internet of Things technologies transmit sensor data to the platform and thereby support monitoring of production status. In the future, artificial intelligence may be applied to demand forecasting and to recommending the most suitable partner. Results. As a result of the study, an information model and a functional structure of a digital platform for managing industrial cooperation were proposed. The model integrates data on enterprises, products, orders, production capacities, and logistics in a single information environment. The criteria-based algorithm makes it possible to filter enterprises that meet the requirements of an order and to recommend them on the basis of a ranking. The accuracy and economic efficiency of the algorithm should be assessed by testing the approach on data from real enterprises. Conclusion. The proposed information model helps to unite the main participants of regional industrial cooperation in a single digital environment. The platform makes it possible to search for enterprises, manage orders, analyse production capacities, and monitor logistics processes. Integrating the platform with electronic contracts, digital payments, artificial intelligence, predictive analytics, and Internet of Things technologies would further expand its functionality. At the same time, information security, data protection, and user authentication require particular attention during practical implementation.

Regional research and innovation agencies are responsible for monitoring large volumes of innovation data submitted by local government units. Non-standardized submissions, manually matched collaboration opportunities, and a growing data request burden have left this data underutilized for policymaking. This study aimed to design, implement, and evaluate an integrated platform for regional innovation monitoring at the Regional Research and Innovation Agency (BRIDA) of East Java Province, using a design and development research approach. The platform combines a clustering based recommendation model that groups semantically similar innovations using multilingual sentence embeddings, an AI chatbot built on Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) for querying the innovation database, and descriptive analytical reports on innovation maturity. Tested on 643 innovation records, the platform achieved a 100 percent functional pass rate across 35 test scenarios, while the chatbot achieved mean faithfulness and relevance scores of 4.0 out of 5.0 under an LLM as a judge evaluation. These results suggest that embedding based clustering can reveal previously hidden collaboration opportunities, while a generative chatbot can meaningfully reduce manual search workload. To the authors' knowledge, this is the first platform integrating clustering based recommendation with RAG based querying for regional innovation monitoring, offering a replicable design for similar settings.

This study aims to develop stem learning system, and let the system become intelligent. We adopt the swarm intelligence and active Ultra-High Frequency RFID for stem learning system, and develop friendly hu-man-computer-interface software for users use the personal digital assistants, personal computers or notebooks. documents.abstract: The article examines the features, priority goals, and risks of integrating artificial intelligence (AI) technologies into medical education. The work examines how future doctors implement digital tools in their training and assess their role in future practice. A survey of 79 4th and 6th year students of the Ternopil National Medical University named after I. Ya. Horbachevsky, who study “Obstetrics and Gynecology”, revealed a paradox. On the one hand, AI has become a part of daily routine for 67.1 % of respondents, another 31.6 % turn to it several times a week. The main advantage is the optimization of time spent: 97.5 % of respondents confirmed significant resource savings. However, the implementation is superficial, as 100 % rely on general-purpose text language models (ChatGPT, Claude) rather than specialized medical software. Expert assistants (UpToDate, Glass AI) are integrated by only 8.9 % of respondents, and image generation programs by 6.3 %. It was found that 83.5 % of students turn to AI to search for clinical protocols; 67.1 % to prepare for the KROK/OSKI exams; 67.1 % to solve clinical problems or write case histories, and only 17.7 % to translate articles. An important aspect was the analysis of self-assessment of prompting skills on a 5-point scale: 12.7 % of students rated them 5 points, 36.7 % rated them 4 points, 46.8 % rated them 3 points, and 3.8 % rated them 2 points. Despite high confidence, 93.7 % of respondents personally encountered AI “hallucinations” – the generation of non-existent facts. Future doctors are clearly aware of the risks of degradation of clinical thinking (63.3 %, n = 50), getting used to “easy answers” (65.3 %, n = 52), and unconscious assimilation of false information (43.0 %, n = 34). The introduction of mandatory discipline in medical AI was fully supported by 23.4 % (n = 18) of respondents, actively supported with reservations by 18.2 % (n = 14), and taken in a neutral position by 45.5 % (n = 35). Based on the data obtained, it is concluded that medical students demonstrate a high intensity of AI use against the background of a critical shortage of work with profile software and a high frequency of encounters with neural network errors. The results justify the need for a strategic transformation of higher medical education – a transition from ignoring technology to the implementation of systematic training in medical prompting, data verification methodology, and digital hygiene for the safe use of AI in future practice.

documents.abstract: This article examines the impacts of generative artificial intelligence on digital game design creation, investigating how this technology transforms creative processes in the industry. The research, using a qualitative approach, employed bibliographic review, comparative case study between Palworld and Pokémon Scarlet and Violet, and semi-structured interviews with three professionals in the field. The analysis identified five thematic categories: technological democratization, transformation of creative processes, preservation of human authenticity, ethical issues, and professional adaptation. The results show that generative AI democratizes game development, allowing independent studios to achieve quality comparable to major producers, but raises questions about authenticity and ethical sustainability. As a practical contribution, the study proposes seven guidelines for maintaining human-centered design, balancing technological innovation with ethical values and human creativity.

documents.abstract: Digital finance has enabled faster payments, lending and banking and investment service, but it has also created a larger attack surface for financial crime, anomaly abuse, money laundering and fraud. This chapter explores intelligent defence mechanisms, which integrate machine learning, deep learning, graph analytics, and explainable artificial intelligence and can identify, interpret, and prevent financial irregularities. It takes a different approach to fraud management, seeing it as a managed decision-making process, and not just a classification exercise. The chapter examines supervised, unsupervised, sequential, graph-based and hybrid methods, explores data imbalance, concept drift, adversarial manipulation, privacy and regulatory accountability, and presents a framework for the implementation of trustworthy fraud intelligence. The chapter is designed for financial crime compliance officers, financial technology developers, and financial institutions looking for comprehensive, auditable, and scalable financial crime prevention systems that leverage AI technology.

Amidst growing uncertainty regarding global sustainable development goals and the increasing complexity of social systems, accurately characterizing long-term transition processes driven by the interactions of multiple agents and factors remains a critical challenge. Using China’s energy transition toward carbon neutrality as a proof-of-concept case, this paper constructs a bidirectional coupling framework based on a hybrid Artificial Intelligence–System Dynamics (AI-SD) approach. Within this framework, an axiomatic SD formal system imposes hard constraints on the nonlinear learning processes of the AI, while the nonlinear corrections generated by the AI feed back to modify the system dynamics structure, thereby establishing an iterative cycle of structural constraints, data-driven corrections, and re-imposed structural constraints. Simulation results demonstrate that the hybrid AI-SD model exhibits good comprehensive adaptability in historical fitting and long-term scenario extrapolation, preserving the system feedback structure while characterizing certain nonlinear and time-delay features. The multi-policy synergy scenario, under the conditions set in this paper, shows a high cumulative emission reduction level and exhibits a relatively coordinated characteristic between emission reduction effects and comprehensive social costs. Model-based sensitivity and attribution analyses indicate that, within the defined parameter space, cumulative technology investment and energy cost conditions are associated with higher model output sensitivity; the contribution of carbon pricing shows a certain scenario dependence. This study provides a computable axiomatic framework for the deep integration of mechanistic models and data-driven approaches, and offers theoretical reference for long-term energy governance and complex system decision optimization under deep uncertainty.

The exponential growth of digital imaging modalities like CT, MRI, Ultrasound, PET and digital pathology has produced huge amount of high dimensional data. This data having powerful insights need advanced computational techniques for accurate interpretation and clinical decision making. In the clinical setting, sophisticated computational analysis models play an important role in supporting correct diagnosis, the monitoring of disease progression, and the treatment decision. The chapter starts with an explanation of the development of medical image analysis from the traditional image processing methods to the modern ML models. Core tasks such as image acquisition modelling, pre-processing, segmentation, registration, feature extraction, classification and quantitative assessment are systematically described. Particular attention is given towards integrating radiomics and artificial intelligence approaches. In addition to methodological foundations, the chapter covers practical considerations such as data variability, multimodal integration, reproducibility, validation strategies and regulatory aspects. Emerging trends such as self-supervised learning, federated learning, explainable artificial intelligence, and foundation models are introduced in this book as well to give readers a window into the future of the field. Overall this chapter provides a conceptual and technical framework for the understanding of computational medical imaging. It provides a basic reference for researchers, graduate students and clinicians who wish to work with advanced image analysis methodologies.

documents.abstract: Metals occupy a unique and often paradoxical position at the interface between human health and the environment. Essential metals such as iron, zinc, copper, magnesium, and molybdenum are indispensable for numerous biological processes, yet their deficiency or excess can lead to serious health consequences. In contrast, toxic metals including lead, mercury, cadmium, and arsenic can cause severe neurological, renal, cardiovascular, and carcinogenic effects, even at very low concentrations. Their persistence in the environment, together with bioaccumulation and biomagnification, further amplifies their impact on ecosystems and human populations. This introductory chapter presents the “good, the bad, and the ugly” of metals, providing an overview of their essential biological functions, toxicological effects, environmental contamination, and long-term ecological consequences. It also highlights recent advances in metal detection, quantification, remediation, and therapeutic intervention, including chemosensors, biosensors, nanotechnology, bioremediation, phytomining, chelation therapy, metallomics, gene editing, and artificial intelligence. Together, these approaches illustrate the need for an integrated and multidisciplinary strategy to maximize the beneficial roles of metals while minimizing their adverse effects on human health and the environment.

BACKGROUND: Telemedicine in intensive care medicine has not yet been uniformly defined or standardized in its implementation in Germany. While the evidence predominantly comes from nonrandomized US studies, German randomized controlled studies (RCT) show potential for improving guideline-compliant treatment. The aim is to develop a consensus-based core data set that standardizes teleconsultations, strengthens data-based care processes and enables future artificial intelligence (AI)-supported analyses. METHOD: The Delphi study, conducted according to the CREDES standard, comprised three rounds with a panel of experts from the German Society of Anesthesiology and Intensive Care Medicine. Documentation templates were extracted, parameters catalogued and iteratively evaluated. Consensus threshold-controlled inclusion or exclusion. Anonymized data analysis was performed descriptively using Excel, supplemented by approval rates and consensus levels. RESULTS: In the first round, 8 of the 12 participants (66.6%) submitted their documentation templates. The initial catalogue created on this basis contained 95 parameters (e.g., patient name, body temperature, mean arterial pressure), which the steering committee classified into 16 categories, such as consultation-related data, imaging and diagnostics, or laboratory values. In the second round, feedback was received from all participants (12/12, 100%) of the expert panel. After applying the exclusion criteria, 7 parameters were removed from the catalogue and 37 new parameters were added. These 125 parameters were then reassigned by the steering group to the categories formed in the first round. In the third round evaluation of the remaining 125 parameters was received from 10 of the 12 participants (83.3%) of the expert panel. Of these, 31 parameters (24.8%) were excluded, 73 (58.4%) were classified as optional and 21 parameters (16.8%) were classified as mandatory. The consensus level rose from 75% to 90%. All categories achieved stable consensus values, thus fulfilling the termination criterion of content saturation. CONCLUSION: This consensus-based core data set could contribute to consistent and reproducible documentation of telemedicine consultations. Also, a mandatory integration of the required parameters into existing clinical documentation systems as well as the early adaptation of technical interfaces, are further key prerequisites for sustainable implementation. Beyond implementation, the catalogue can support harmonization among Tele-ICU networks, facilitate the benchmarking of consultation processes and provide a structured foundation for future multicenter analyses. In particular, the distinction between mandatory and optional parameters enables a pragmatic balance between clinical relevance, documentation burden and local technical readiness. Consistent use of the core data set supports guideline-based processes, improves comparability across sites and can contribute to the development of future quality indicators and AI-supported analyses.

Deep learning has made significant advancements in medical data analysis, which has made it possible to advance the diagnostics process, prognostication, and therapeutic care through new methods. However, the usability of artificial neural networks in common clinical practice is still hindered by their excessive computational, memory, and power requirements, which do not make them applicable to the resource-stressed conditions of a portable imaging device, a wearable sensor, or an edge-computing system. The limitations are dealt with in this chapter by discussing ways of making medical neural networks more efficient. The question of interest is model-compression methods such as pruning, quantization, knowledge distillation, and neural architecture search, aimed at reducing the computational cost while preserving diagnostic quality. Also, the chapter argues for improvements in training time, which include transfer learning, self-supervised learning, and few-shot learning, which alleviate the challenges posed by small labeled medical datasets. The previous sections have discussed highly effective architectures, such as MobileNet, ShuffleNet and EfficientNet, that offer promising trade-offs in accuracy and efficiency in various medical uses including imaging, biomedical signal processing, and multimodal healthcare. Their practical usefulness is empirically demonstrated in case studies of quantised convolutional neural networks to screen X-rays, quantised networks to monitor ECGs, and distilled networks for mobile ultrasound devices. A comparison of the trade-offs between accuracy and efficiency, interpretability and ethical deployment confirms the need to use lightweight neural networks in real-time medical artificial intelligence systems that are deployable and scalable.

The use of Large Language Models in computer science education has produced a fast-growing body of primary studies. Existing secondary studies tend to categorise this literature by external criteria, such as the model used, the course it operates in, or the benefit it reports; the educational artefact itself is discussed but not adopted as the unit of analysis. This study adopts it: the LLM-enabled educational artefact (LEEA), a deliverable built on an LLM for educational purposes, either technological, such as a tool, system, or agent, or methodological, such as a model or technique, rather than the general-purpose model that powers it. Through a review of scientific databases, 158 primary studies published between 2022 and February 2025 were analysed using a six-dimensional codification scheme and six research questions. The mapped studies concentrate on a few options: 69.6% of contributions focus on tools and systems, 84.8% rely on the GPT family, and 86.1% target undergraduate education. Feedback appears in 76.6% of studies, while other instructional stages remain underexplored. Evidence comes mainly from user perception and system performance, which rarely overlap; only 21.5% of studies measure learning gains, so the evidence on learning remains limited. The study contributes a multidimensional map of this literature and a codification scheme detailing eleven educational functions and seven families of effectiveness metrics derived from the corpus.

documents.abstract: Highly sophisticated phishing and social engineering attacks, along with newly emerging forms of digital threats, need to be countered with the aid of large language models (LLMs). Conventional security mechanisms usually fail to combat new and subtle frauds, but LLCMs offer a considerable benefit due to the superior capability to process and comprehend multi-purpose and multi-faceted human-like language. The models are capable of identifying the fine grains of information, unusual trends and ill motives that will pass even basic filters because they read enormous volumes of text messages in email messages, web pages, and security logs. By examining such factors as tone, urgency, grammatical irregularities, and inconsistencies of context, they may be used to categorise the threats with maximum accuracy, which may provide an essential defence angle against the attacks based on the manipulation of the psychological processes. In addition to being detected, LLMs are also capable of giving explanations to human readers on the reasons behind their decisions, and thus, black box security systems have become transparent and can be used by human reviewers. Their adaptability and the ability to learn constantly are the secrets to their success since security structures act proactively to prevent the emergence of attack vectors. Even though they do introduce certain additional problems, e.g., weakness to adversarial attacks and the necessity to handle computational expenditures with care, integration will be at the centre in developing more robust, adaptive, and intelligent information security countermeasures within our increasingly threatened cyberspace.

This paper explores the intersection of logic and narratology in Noel Carroll's theory of narrative closure (2007). Grounding his theory in the logic of questions and answers, technically known as inferential erotetic logic, Carroll built his theory on the concept of the erotetic narrative, which employs, according to inferential logic, causal narrative connections to pose questions to the reader as a means to process the narrative cognitively. According to Carroll, narrative closure occurs when these questions are answered, manifesting as a phenomenological feeling experienced by the reader. This paper identifies a critical gap in Carroll's theory, which is the omission of logical inference in achieving narrative closure. By omitting the role of inference, Carroll's theory reduces closure to a purely plot-driven process, overlooking the cognitive mechanisms through which readers generate and resolve questions. This paper argues that the re-institution of inference in Carroll’s theory offers a more comprehensive understanding of how narrative closure functions, extending beyond the plot to include the reader's active engagement in question generation and resolution.

With the diffusion of generative AI, AI emotional companion apps have emerged as a new domain of digital consumption in which users may pay to extend relationship-like experiences. This study examines how loneliness and actual-ideal self-discrepancy are associated with experience-enhancing consumption intention and continuance intention through two competing pathways: emotional bonding with the AI (relational compensation) and escapism (avoidant compensation). The emotional bond with the AI is modeled as a second-order construct comprising anthropomorphism, emotional responsiveness, and parasocial intimacy. Data were collected from 393 adult users in China who used AI emotional companion apps at least twice per week and were analyzed using structural equation modeling. Loneliness and actual-ideal self-discrepancy were positively associated with both emotional bonding and escapism. However, significant indirect associations with experience-enhancing consumption intention and continuance intention emerged only through the emotional-bond pathway. Direct comparisons further showed that the relational indirect effects were significantly stronger than the avoidant indirect effects across all antecedent–outcome combinations. Escapism was significantly associated with both outcomes when modeled alone but became nonsignificant when emotional bonding was included, suggesting that its association with consumer responses largely overlaps with the relational pathway. A partial-mediation analysis further showed that actual-ideal self-discrepancy retained a significant direct association with continuance intention. These findings suggest that relational compensation, rather than avoidant compensation, is more closely associated with willingness to pay for experience enhancement and intention to continue using AI companions. The study extends compensatory-use, self-discrepancy, and parasocial-interaction perspectives to the AI-companion context by linking psychological vulnerability to experience-enhancing consumption intention and continuance intention, while highlighting implications for responsible relational design and user protection.

documents.abstract: The early identification of students who are likely to experience academic failure has become an important application of machine learning (ML) and learning analytics in higher education. Although numerous studies have developed predictive models for student performance, the literature remains fragmented across performance prediction, at-risk identification, dropout prediction, and student success modelling, with substantial variation in outcome definitions, predictor availability, validation strategies, and evaluation metrics. This systematic literature review synthesizes research on ML-based prediction of student academic outcomes, with particular emphasis on failure-oriented and early-warning applications. A PRISMA-aligned evidence-synthesis strategy was used to examine systematic reviews, empirical studies, established educational datasets, and recent developments in explainable and responsible artificial intelligence. The reviewed evidence indicates that classification-based approaches, particularly decision trees, random forests, support vector machines, logistic regression, artificial neural networks, and ensemble methods, dominate the field. Academic history, assessment performance, learning-management-system activity, attendance, engagement, and demographic or contextual variables are frequently used predictors. However, high predictive accuracy does not necessarily indicate practical usefulness because information leakage, class imbalance, temporal instability, inadequate calibration, limited external validation, and weak interpretability remain important methodological concerns. Recent studies further demonstrate the importance of explainable AI, fairness assessment, privacy-preserving data generation, and temporal modelling. Based on these findings, this study proposes a Failure-Oriented Explainable Temporal Machine Learning Framework (FET-MLF), integrating leakage-aware temporal feature engineering, predictive modelling, probability calibration, explainability, fairness auditing, and intervention feedback. The framework shifts evaluation from accuracy-centric modelling toward trustworthy, actionable, and institutionally deployable early-warning systems for preventing academic failure.

documents.abstract: This study aimed to determine the relationship between the management of educational technology by teachers, the digital literacy of teachers, and student engagement in technology-integrated learning through a descriptive-correlational research design. It was found that student engagement in technology-integrated learning, according to teachers’ perceptions, was characterized by an overall mean score of 2.98 on a four-point rating scale, which was interpreted as “Agree,” and that behavioral engagement (M=3.12) and emotional engagement (M=3.14) were both higher compared to cognitive engagement (M=2.67). There was a significant correlation between the teachers’ perception of the management of educational technology integration and student engagement (r=.30, p<.05), while the digital literacy of teachers had a moderate positive correlation with student engagement (r=.42, p<.05). However, student engagement was assessed through teachers’ perceptions rather than direct student reports or classroom observations, which should be considered when interpreting the findings. Based on the results, a comprehensive intervention plan focusing on professional development, collaborative learning communities, technology support, and continuous monitoring was proposed to strengthen technology integration and student engagement in elementary schools.

Abstract : The growing use of generative artificial intelligence (AI) in education creates a need for assessments that measure teachers’ pedagogical judgement rather than relying solely on self-reported competence. This study developed and examined initial validity evidence for a vignette-based assessment of AI-pedagogical knowledge among pre-service teachers. Instrument development proceeded from construct definition and blueprinting to an initial pool of 36 researcher-developed vignettes, developer screening, a diagnostic pilot with 60 pre-service teachers, systematic item revision, and content review by three independent experts. The revised 24-item assessment was administered to an analytic sample of 484 pre-service teachers. Validity evidence was examined through expert ratings, internal structure, item and distractor functioning, score reliability and conditional precision, differential item functioning, and relations with external variables. Aiken’s V coefficients ranged from .83 to 1.00 (M = .94), although the small expert panel and restricted use of rating categories warrant cautious interpretation. A one-factor model adequately represented the response data, supporting interpretation of a total score rather than separate domain scores (CFI = .990, TLI = .989, RMSEA = .034, SRMR = .065). Internal consistency was high (KR-20 = .93; categorical omega = .95), but precision was concentrated at the lower end of the ability distribution. Of the participants, 24.2% obtained the maximum score and 47.5% scored 22 or higher. No item showed non-negligible differential functioning by gender or field of study. Knowledge scores were moderately associated with AI self-efficacy (r = .36) and teaching self-efficacy (r = .33) and more weakly associated with self-reported instructional practice (r = .22). The assessment may support formative and research uses when interpreted as a single total score, but it is not yet suitable for ranking or high-stakes decisions. Further development requires more difficult items, revision of weak items and distractors, cognitive interviews, and cross-institutional evaluation.

documents.abstract: Money Tree is an ongoing, AI-assisted experimental research program investigating whether reproducible forward-looking information can be detected in chronological systems that are nominally or apparently random. Mega Millions is used as a deliberately difficult experimental target because its outcomes are discrete, chronological, publicly observable, externally generated, and designed to be unpredictable. The objective is not simply to predict lottery numbers. The lottery serves as a stress test for a broader question: can weak forward-looking structure be distinguished from coincidence, false discovery, data leakage, adaptive overfitting, or artifacts created by the way data are represented? The project began in 2026 with a simple historical-frequency question and evolved into a software research laboratory incorporating walk-forward evaluation, matched random controls, Monte Carlo testing, independent analytical engines, falsification procedures, a centralized Referee layer, AI specialist reviews, and prospective high-volume experimentation. This research is being released while it is still in progress. No claim of reliable lottery prediction is made. Positive, negative, inconclusive, and failed experiments are intentionally preserved in the research record. Collaboration is a primary purpose of this release. We welcome researchers, independent investigators, mathematicians, statisticians, software developers, and others working with stochastic processes, sequential prediction, complex systems, information theory, experimental mathematics, random-number testing, anomaly detection, or other noisy chronological systems. We are particularly interested in people who have methods, datasets, criticisms, or ongoing experiments that could independently challenge this framework. We are also interested in helping evaluate outside experiments or datasets where our developing zero-trust, walk-forward, matched-control methodology may be useful. A rigorous demonstration that one of our ideas is wrong is considered a successful contribution. The project was initiated and directed by Troy Stuart, who began without a computer-programming or computer-science background and learned AI prompting, Python development workflows, Visual Studio Code, GitHub, version control, testing, and experimental research practices while building the project step by step. ChatGPT, known throughout the project as “Chappie,” has served as a substantive AI research collaborator in research framing, discussion, drafting, code-oriented guidance, critique, documentation, and coordination of independent AI specialist reviews. Troy Stuart remains the human project originator, decision-maker, and accountable author. Research status: Ongoing.Version: 1.0Release date: October 2, 2026.

ABSTRACT Background Manual prescription of liver MRI volumes introduces inter‐operator variability and prolongs exam duration. Artificial intelligence (AI)‐based prescription has been demonstrated, but existing work has been limited to single‐vendor settings. Purpose To develop and validate an AI model for automated liver MRI prescription using a large, consecutive, multicenter dataset encompassing multiple vendors, field strengths, localizer sequences, and liver pathologies. Study Type Retrospective. Population A total of 11,012 patients (5928 female) who underwent liver MRI exams across three vendors (GE HealthCare, Philips Healthcare, Siemens Healthineers) at three institutions, split into training/validation/test sets (70/10/20%). Liver disorders included cirrhosis, ascites, portal hypertension, and iron overload. Field Strength/Sequence Three‐plane localizers acquired using single‐shot fast spin echo (68.3%) and gradient echo (31.7%) at 1.5 T (52.8%) and 3 T (47.2%). Assessment A YOLOv8 object detection model was trained to detect the liver, torso, and arms on localizer images. Automated prescription accuracy was assessed using three‐dimensional intersection‐over‐union (IoU 3D ) for axial, coronal, and sagittal prescriptions. Subgroup analyses evaluated performance across technical and patient‐related factors. Statistical Tests Mann–Whitney U tests with Bonferroni correction, Kruskal‐Wallis tests, Wilcoxon signed‐rank tests, Spearman correlation. Effect sizes were calculated using rank‐biserial correlation ( r rb ) and epsilon‐squared ( ε 2 ). p < 0.05 was considered statistically significant. Results Median axial prescription IoU 3D was 0.963 (interquartile range: 0.946–0.976), with median IoU 3D above 0.940 for coronal and sagittal prescriptions. For axial prescriptions, margins less than 4 mm in each direction were required to achieve complete coverage of manual prescriptions in 90% of cases in the held‐out test set. Effects were negligible to small across vendors, field strengths, localizer sequences, and patient factors ( r rb ≤ 0.16, ε 2 ≤ 0.01). Data Conclusion A single multivendor model achieved accurate automated liver MRI prescription without clinically meaningful performance differences across vendors, field strengths, localizer sequences, or patient factors. Evidence Level 2. Technical Efficacy Stage 1.

documents.abstract: We present Muslim, a production Arabic voice AI platform serving grounded, sourced Islamic knowledge to real users. Beyond a real-time voice pipeline (NeMo Arabic ASR, an OpenAI-compatible LLM endpoint, self-hosted TTS) and a deterministic multi-source retrieval layer routed across six Model Context Protocol servers, we report three things a research prototype typically lacks. First, a released family of fine-tuned Arabic Islamic model artifacts: an efficient tool-routing LLM (Muslim-6B-PRO, 5.94B parameters) and a Modern Standard Arabic TTS model (Fasih-TTS-V1) that ranks 5th of 17 overall and 2nd of 11 open-weight systems on the community-voted Arabic TTS Arena for MSA. Second, an account and metering layer - a free per-account turn allowance, capacity-aware refusal, and email verification deferred to the point it actually matters - that turns an open demo into an operable, abuse-resistant product. Third, a three-layer observability stack (liveness, error reporting, product analytics) built specifically around the system's characteristic failure mode: a GPU-bound agent host going silent while the web tier keeps serving normally. We report real, measured latency and accuracy figures (98.4% recitation-validation accuracy on 124 cases; end-to-end voice latency of 0.9-1.7s) and discuss the concrete engineering trade-offs and limitations of running an Islamic-knowledge voice product in production.

This review evaluates the performance of natural-zeolite concrete under acidic and sulfate attack. The review discusses the literature on visual deterioration, weight loss, erosion depth, compressive strength retention, service life, and microstructural characteristics. The findings indicate that the durability performance of natural-zeolite concrete depends on the type of aggressive environment and the zeolite replacement level. Under sulfate exposure, natural zeolite improves durability by consuming calcium hydroxide and promoting the formation of additional calcium silicate hydrate (C-S-H) . It also reduces gypsum and ettringite formation, which improves compressive strength retention and extends the service life of concrete. One study showed that 20% zeolite extended service life from 15 to 35 months and maintained more than 75% relative compressive strength after 1050 days of sodium sulfate exposure. The results are study-specific and should not be considered a universal optimum. In contrast, the reported performance under sulfuric acid attack remains inconsistent. However, higher replacement levels (15%–30%) have also been associated with increased surface deterioration and strength loss under severe acid exposure. The review demonstrates that sulfuric acid is more aggressive than hydrochloric acid. However, differences in acid concentration, pH, exposure duration, and solution renewal limit direct comparison. The review also highlights that combining zeolite with tuff can partially mitigate tuff's adverse effects under acidic conditions. In addition, recent advances in artificial intelligence and machine learning demonstrate considerable potential for predicting and optimizing the performance of zeolite concrete by capturing nonlinear relationships. However, applying AI-based approaches to predict sulfuric-acid-induced deterioration and the sulfate resistance of natural-zeolite concrete remains largely unexplored. Conflicting findings among available studies also highlight the need for systematic investigations to establish the optimum zeolite replacement level and identify the governing parameters responsible for variations.

The state of occupational health and safety (OH&S) in Zambia, particularly focusing on small-scale contractors (SSCs), is presented in this chapter, highlighting the country’s economic and labour context and the role of SSCs in the creation of employment and delivery of infrastructure despite limited finance and technical capacity. A review on the registration and grading process under the National Council for Construction is presented with a view to outlining that most SSCs in Zambia that operate in lower grades experience restricted access to high-value contracts, which often results in subcontracting with other capable, larger companies. An analysis of the legal and regulatory framework that establishes employers’ and employees’ duties and responsibilities, compensation mechanisms, and environmental safeguards and their enforcement, which remain inconsistent, has been outlined. The chapter highlights a critical OH&S Policy established under the Occupational Health and Safety Act 16 of 2025 that enables employers to ensure that the working environments are safe and to undertake health risk assessments. Gaps in the legal framework are that their complexity leads to failure to comply by SSCs in terms of inadequate awareness and training, limited access to OH&S services, especially for the SSCs working in rural Zambia, and a lack of technical skills. Zambia, on one hand, has ratified some of the International Labour Organisation (ILO) conventions that also contribute to the OH&S oversight, thus showing willingness to improve the safety and health of workplaces by this recognition of global standards.

In this chapter, focused representative cases were selected to explore occupational health and safety (OH&S) performance management in developing countries, Ghana, and South Africa. Although these countries possess unique systems, they share common problems that crosscut small-scale contractors (SSCs) in industries like energy, oil, gas, and construction where these contractors dominate but have inadequate capacity to effectively manage OH&S. Elevated accidents, injuries and fatality are recorded attributable to inadequate skills, weak communication systems, insufficient regulatory compliance, corruption, and limited resources, which collectively lead to under-reporting of incidents, hindering effective implementation of interventions. While globalisation and rapid industrialisation add to the risks, the inherited legal systems, fragmented policies, and inadequate institutional capacity have continued to direct OH&S systems. The chapter expounds on how Ghana has illustrated progress in line with the development of legislative initiatives for SSCs, with no coherent OH&S policy. South Africa reflects a more robust legal framework while encountering enforcement gaps. The International Labour Organisation (ILO) conventions and the Southern African Development Community (SADCC) convention are informing regional initiatives on the significance of streamlined OH&S standards, improved collection of data, and improved cooperation among stakeholders. This chapter underscores the development of an integrated framework that supports awareness, training, and reduced incidents to ensure workers’ safety. Sub-Saharan African countries, including Zambia, can operationalise lessons to develop OH&S initiatives for safer, sustainable workplaces.

In recent years, occupational health and safety (OH&S) performance management has been gaining recognition as an important driver in attaining sustainable development with the view of assisting small-scale contractors (SSCs) who are in environments that are resource-strained. Therefore, this chapter analyses the OH&S performance management conceptual perspective relationship with the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), the process of measurement, indicators to be adopted, and the frameworks. Evidently, inadequate OH&S exposes employees to hazardous conditions that lead to reduced productivity and eventually reinforce poverty. Conversely, this chapter illustrates how effective OH&S performance management supports SDGs 1, 3, and 8 on poverty reduction, health and well-being, and decent work and economic growth, respectively, by highlighting the significance of OH&S measurement through outcome indicators and positive performance indicators (PPIs). These outcomes and indicators promote audits, identification of hazards, and assessment of safety culture. By incorporating PPIs with outcome indicators, continuous improvement, safety at the workplace, and well-being for employees can be achieved. Ultimately, this chapter reinforces that resilient OH&S performance management is fundamental in ensuring that the workers are safe by reducing the rate of accidents and fostering sustainable economic growth.

Engineering laboratories combine high-energy machinery, live circuits, pressurised fluids and open flames with novice student operators, yet occupational health and safety in Indonesian higher education is still managed largely through academic rather than risk-based instruments. This study applies Hazard Identification, Risk Assessment and Risk Control (HIRARC) to six practicum laboratories of the Department of Mechanical and Industrial Engineering, Universitas Tidar, using the practicum activity rather than the room as the unit of analysis. Hazards were identified through direct observation and document review and scored by an assessor panel on a 5 x 5 matrix with predefined severity and likelihood criteria. Three main findings emerge. First, the 27 activity-level hazards are dominated by mechanical sources, and nearly half of the activities (44%) are high risk before control. Second, risk profiles differ between laboratories: the machining-intensive Production Process, Welding and CNC laboratories carry the highest mean risk, while the single most severe activity is CNC operation with a running spindle, so mean-based and peak-based rankings point to different priorities. Third, combined engineering and administrative controls, each mapped to the Indonesian regulation that requires it, are expected by the assessor panel to bring every activity to the low band, an estimated mean reduction of 58.5%; this is a prospective panel estimate, not a result measured after implementation. The study contributes an activity-based, regulation-linked risk register that allows laboratories with different energy profiles to be compared on one scale and to be prioritised for safety investment.

Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly reshaping qualitative research, quantitative research, and mixed methods research, but practical guidance for conducting, evaluating, and reporting human–AI analytic collaboration remains underdeveloped. Building on AI-augmented transformatizing, a representational–recursive framework that conceptualizes AI as a participant in analytic re-representation rather than merely as a technical tool, this article advances a practice-oriented framework for Human-AI Augmented Mixed Methods Research. The article offers three integrated contributions. First, it proposes the AI-Augmented Transformatizing Protocol , a recursive workflow for preparing representations, for assigning human and AI analytic roles, for generating AI-assisted transformations, for conducting human critique, for refining findings, and for constructing meta-inferences. Second, it introduces quality criteria for assessing methodological rigor in human-AI augmented analysis, including representational fidelity, prompt traceability, recursive transparency, human oversight integrity, algorithmic reflexivity, convergence-divergence interrogation, meta-inferential robustness, and ethical accountability. Third, it presents reporting standards designed to help authors disclose AI systems, model versions, prompting procedures, analytic iterations, researcher interventions, validation/legitimation strategies, ethical safeguards, and limitations. These proposed methodological components are conceptual and practice-oriented rather than empirically validated; accordingly, the worked example illustrates their operational logic, whereas future research is needed to establish their empirical performance, including the validity and reliability of the HAAM-QAM. Rather than treating AI use as an optional efficiency enhancement, the framework positions human-AI collaboration as a structured methodological practice requiring explicit design, documentation, reflexivity, and accountability. By translating the theory of AI-augmented transformatizing into protocols, quality criteria, and reporting standards, this article provides methodologists, researchers, authors, reviewers, editors, graduate educators, mentors, and the like with practical guidance for conducting transparent, rigorous, and ethically responsible AI-augmented mixed methods research in psychology and related fields. In so doing, it extends current reporting guidelines and quality frameworks by addressing the distinctive representational, recursive, and ethical demands introduced when AI participates directly in analysis.

BACKGROUND: Infection remains the second leading cause of death in patients with ESKD on hemodialysis. This exploratory analysis sought to characterize interruptions and non-routine events (NREs), in the outpatient dialysis setting, with particular interest in the relationships between interruptions and NREs and infection prevention and control (IPC) activities. METHODS: We conducted a mixed-methods, observational, exploratory study of 45 patients and their dialysis teams across four U.S. dialysis facilities (99 total outpatient hemodialysis treatments hours observed). Structured observations were focused on the team surrounding an individual patient for the duration of their dialysis session using a modified Line Operations Safety Audit (LOSA) approach. Quantitative analyses were conducted. RESULTS: A technician simultaneously caring for four patients can experience a median of 64 interruptions, or 16 per patient (range 3-50) during their treatment time. The phases with greatest risk of infection (i.e., connection, disconnection) had a significantly higher time required to complete (with NRE: connection 14:37, disconnection 13:41; without NRE: connection 7:32, disconnection 8:18). Thirty-seven of 45 patients experienced at least one NRE during clinical care, defined as a patient-related clinical event (e.g., long clotting time) or an operational variation (e.g., transportation problem). Findings are exploratory in nature and provide support for future hypothesis generation and testing. CONCLUSIONS: Interruptions and NREs were frequent in the outpatient dialysis work system, and connection and disconnection times were longer when an NRE was present. Since these disruptions occurred during phases that include IPC-related activities, they may introduce competing demands that could challenge consistent adherence, though adherence was not directly measured. These exploratory findings may inform the design of workflows and processes that better support IPC and patient safety in the outpatient dialysis setting.

This study aims to analyze the influence of Generative AI usage on the learning independence of Generation Z students at STIT Darul Ulum Kotabaru, viewed from the perspective of perceived ease of use and potential dependency. The research employs a quantitative approach with an associative causal design. Data were collected through questionnaires distributed to Generation Z students who have used Generative AI in academic activities. The variables examined include perceived ease of use of Generative AI (X1), potential dependency on Generative AI (X2), and student learning independence (Y). Data analysis was conducted using multiple linear regression with SPSS. The results indicate that perceived ease of use and potential dependency simultaneously influence students' learning independence. Generative AI provides significant convenience in accessing information, understanding materials, and completing academic tasks. However, excessive use without critical thinking and academic responsibility can lead to dependency that reduces learning independence. This study contributes to the development of educational technology studies, particularly in understanding the impact of Generative AI on student learning behavior in Islamic higher education institutions

Diabetes mellitus merupakan gangguan metabolik kronis yang membutuhkan deteksi dini agar komplikasi jangka panjang dapat dicegah sejak awal. Penelitian ini membandingkan kinerja prediktif dua algoritma klasifikasi berbasis pohon, yaitu Decision Tree dan Random Forest, dalam mendeteksi diabetes pada tahap awal menggunakan dataset Pima Indians Diabetes dari UCI Machine Learning Repository. Sebagai pelengkap, penelitian ini juga menerapkan kerangka Explainable Artificial Intelligence lima lapis yang memanfaatkan SHAP guna menghasilkan penjelasan model yang relevan secara klinis, mulai dari kepentingan fitur global hingga validasi terhadap pengetahuan patofisiologi. Rekayasa fitur dilakukan untuk memperluas ruang fitur dari 8 menjadi 14 variabel, sementara tahap praproses meliputi stratified train-test split, imputasi median, winsorizing berbasis IQR, normalisasi Min-Max, dan SMOTE untuk menyeimbangkan distribusi kelas yang tidak proporsional. Optimasi hyperparameter dilakukan melalui GridSearchCV dengan Stratified K-Fold sebanyak lima lipatan, menggunakan F1-Score sebagai kriteria utama. Hasil eksperimen menunjukkan bahwa Random Forest secara konsisten mengungguli Decision Tree pada seluruh metrik evaluasi, dengan F1-Score cross-validation sebesar 0,9002 berbanding 0,8687 dan ROC-AUC pada set pengujian sebesar 80,61% berbanding 70,43%. McNemar Test menunjukkan bahwa perbedaan pola kesalahan klasifikasi antar kedua model tidak signifikan secara statistik pada ukuran sampel yang tersedia, namun pertimbangan multidimensional seperti stabilitas cross-validation dan selisih ROC-AUC tetap mendukung rekomendasi terhadap Random Forest. Analisis SHAP mengonfirmasi bahwa Insulin, Glucose, dan rasio Insulin terhadap Glucose merupakan tiga prediktor paling berpengaruh, sejalan dengan mekanisme patofisiologi diabetes tipe 2 yang telah mapan dalam literatur kedokteran. Penelitian ini juga mengakui keterbatasan generalisabilitas dataset terhadap populasi Indonesia sebagai catatan penting bagi penelitian lanjutan.
